Main Trends of Spanish IT-Sector

The Spanish IT market has gone through significant developments in recent years. With a growth rate of 7.28% since 2023, it’s not showing any signs of slowing down. By 2028, it will surpass $31 billion in volume, contributing to the country’s economic progress.

This substantial market growth caused the number of Spanish IT companies to increase. Currently, about 23,000 such entities are offering their comprehensive services and qualified developers in Spain.

Software Development Nearshoring in Spain

Speaking of software developers and other IT specialists, their number already exceeds 333,000. Even so, Spain faces severe talent scarcity, with IT and technology being the most sought-after profession. As a result, many Spanish business owners are looking for tech experts abroad. They hire developers in Belgium, France, the UK, the Netherlands, or Ukraine to fill in the gaps in their companies.

Despite the Spanish IT sector’s obstacles, its tech export value has seen remarkable success. Following World Bank data, it jumped from $13.55 billion in 2011 to a spectacular $23.46 billion in 2021, indicating the competitiveness and global reach of IT services in Spain. Using well-known programming languages like PHP, .NET, Lua, Python, and Java improves the industry’s performance even further. To hire developers in Belgium, France, UK, Netherlands can be a solution for a Spanish IT company that is looking for good specialists.

Since Spain is an attractive country for tourism, IT achievements are implemented in this sphere as well. Modern technologies are used to control air flights and other means of transport, according to the MIT Technology Review.

Spain’s English Proficiency Index score of 545, indicating “Moderate Proficiency,” reflects the country’s solid foundation in English language skills while leaving room for further improvement in communication and global opportunities.

An Overview of Spain’s Employment Conditions

Spain’s employment landscape features a rich diversity of industries, including tourism, manufacturing, agriculture and renewable energy. The country’s fantastic location and cultural heritage contribute to a flourishing tourism sector. Additionally, Spain has experienced notable growth in its renewable energy industry.

Payroll in the country typically follows a monthly schedule. And salaries are commonly paid at the end of each month. Employers are required to follow with specific payroll taxes, such as contributions towards social security, healthcare and other statutory benefits. These contributions quite greatly influence the overall cost of labor for businesses. Consequently, this impacts their financial operations and budgeting.

The minimum wage in Spain is flexible to periodic adjustments. It aims to support the well-being of employees. Currently, the minimum salary stands at approximately $1,080 per month. And, this is quite high! Overtime pay is overseen by labor laws and ensures that employees receive fair compensation.

Employee benefits form an integral part of the employment framework in Spain. Many companies offer comprehensive health insurance, paid leave and retirement plans to attract and retain skilled workers. These benefits are designed to enhance employee satisfaction. It also promotes a healthy work-life balance, and supports a positive work culture within organizations.

Core IT Hubs in Spain

Several Spanish cities largely contribute to the country’s IT sector. Let’s explore each of them in greater detail.

  • Madrid. The capital of Spain is a hotspot for software developers owing to its booming IT, logistics, and eCommerce industries. It proudly houses the country’s largest data centers, with a whopping $6.72 million investment planned for their expansion. Notably, the city will welcome the first-ever Oracle Cloud Infrastructure in the region. To hire software developers Madrid costs around $77,467 per year.
  • Barcelona. Known for its thriving tech scene, it’s another major hub for software development in Spain. With over 2,000 startups and counting, the city’s startup ecosystem is flourishing and constantly expanding. Companies aiming to hire software developers Barcelona expect to pay around $75,555 annually.
  • Valencia. As the top-third city for startups in Spain, with 94 thriving companies as of 2023, it’s a promising destination for IT specialists. Businesses determined to hire software developers Valencia should expect to pay about $62,094 yearly.
  • Sevilla. Located in south Spain, this city is making strides in the IT sector and holds the fifth place for startups. Software developers in this region make about $65,261 per year.
  • Zaragoza. Established itself with an advanced smart city infrastructure, it is another center for software development. The developer’s salary in Zaragoza is around $68,270 yearly.

Using a Nearshore Spain Dedicated Team

One of the most popular models for development is to hire an entire team of IT professionals to undertake all aspects of the required work. IT nearshoring Madrid will allow you to access a full range of IT professionals that will work solely on the tasks that you have.

Using a nearshore Spain dedicated team is often the most effective way of getting your projects completed just as you require. This is because they will be focused on the work that you need doing and nothing else. However, this can be a costly way forward, especially with IT wages within Spain being higher than in some other countries.

Skills shortages within the country and a high cost of living drive up wages making hiring teams within the country an expensive proposition. However, with IT you are not limited to only using those that can be hired locally.

Basic Requirements for a Programmer to Join Spain Dedicated Team

Despite the confident development of the Information and Communication Technology sector (ICT), it is not an easy task to work as a SW developer in Spain, especially for foreign citizens. The main reason for this is the fact that many Spanish IT companies require potential candidates to speak Spanish, in addition to basic English, as reported by Justlanded.com. The matter is further complicated by the fact that different dialects of Spanish are used in different regions of the country.

The complicated procedure for obtaining a work visa also stands in the way of those who are looking for a job in the IT sector of this country. Thus, at the moment, Spain is kind of a vicious circle. On the one hand, there is a shortage of own specialists, and on the other, foreign experts are rarely hired.

Nevertheless, businesses look for all possible solutions for their projects and very often choose IT staffing or offshore development companies who look for needed programmers with Spanish speaking skills and wish to create Spain dedicated team.

FAQs

  • What opportunities does the Spanish market offer for foreign businesses?

At the crossroads of innovation and commerce, Spain beckons foreign businesses with its thriving IT domain, unmatched tech exports on the global scale, and tech-centric cities such as Madrid and Barcelona. The added bonus of high English proficiency positions Spain as a hub for industry alliances and business development.

  • What challenges does Spain face in terms of local tech talent?

Despite having over 333,000 IT specialists, Spain grapples with a severe talent shortage in the tech sector. This has led many Spanish businesses to seek tech experts from countries like Belgium, France, the UK, the Netherlands, and Ukraine.

  • In the Spanish IT arena, which cities are considered prominent?

The heartbeat of Spain’s IT sector resonates strongly in cities like Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla, and Zaragoza, all of which are hubs for booming IT activities, emergent startup landscapes, and forward-thinking tech infrastructure projects.

  • Do Companies Require Spanish Language Proficiency?

Spanish IT enterprises frequently look for bilingual candidates, emphasizing proficiency in Spanish and a foundational understanding of English. This is further complemented by the range of Spanish dialects spoken across the nation.

  • How do the salaries of developers in Spain compare with those in other countries like Ukraine?

A software developer in Spain typically earns around $3,500 per month, while the average salary for a developer in Ukraine is about $2,000 per month, making it a more cost-effective option for businesses considering outsourcing.
